question: Ingrid grows more sunflowers than her neighbour Bo does. She started with 236 seedlings, and 157 were lost to slugs. Bo gave her 42 seedlings from his own tray. Every seedling she had left went on to produce 6 flower heads. Wind snapped 207 of the flower heads before the show. How many flower heads does Ingrid have?

A hospital radio station had 149 records in its cabinet, and a listener donated 69 more. A burst pipe destroyed 197 records. The station then made 7 digital copies of every record that survived. A volunteer added 34 copies from her own collection, a college sent 45, and a local band contributed 35. Half of the cabinet is now taken up by cables. How many copies does the station have?

A bus depot began the month with 158 timetable boards. The design team took 25 boards away to be redrawn. A printer delivered 51 new boards, and 17 boards were damaged by vandals. The council then ordered a complete set for each of the 7 routes, using that many boards per route. Half of the depot yard is given over to parking, and the timetables are printed in hours although the drivers work to minutes. How many boards were ordered altogether?

On Monday morning Ludo had 67 trays of bedding plants, more than his colleague Sanne had prepared. Each tray held 7 plants. Before noon 102 plants were sold. In the afternoon Sanne added 59 plants to the bench, and a delivery brought 51 more. In the evening head office ordered that same display for each of its 4 garden centres, needing that many plants per centre. The centres advertise opening times in hours although the staff rotas are written in minutes. How many plants are needed altogether?

On Saturday morning a bike shop had 213 inner tubes in stock. A cycling club bought 203 tubes before lunch. In the early afternoon 9 tubes were found to be perished and were binned. In the evening the wholesaler delivered 5 tubes for every tube still in the shop. Overnight head office repeated that delivery at each of its 7 branches, sending that many tubes to every branch. The shop quotes repair times in minutes although its adverts give them in hours. How many tubes were sent to the branches altogether?

Ottilie carves more spoons than her apprentice Nils does. She had 158 blocks of wood, and 56 of them were too knotty to use. Each usable block was cut into 9 spoon blanks. The blanks were shared equally between the 3 benches in the workshop, and Ottilie's bench is the one being followed. Every blank at her bench was then whittled into 8 small tasting spoons, and a craft fair sold 2085 of those spoons. How many spoons are left at Ottilie's bench?

On Friday morning Bea had 216 jars of pickles on her shelves, more than her supplier Ferdi carried in his van. He delivered 55 jars before opening. During the morning 198 jars were sold, and in the early afternoon 52 jars went out to a restaurant. In the evening Ferdi restocked the shop with 6 jars for every jar still on the shelf. Bea's sister then added 79 jars she had made at home. How many jars are in the shop now?

Tanya's cafe has more chairs than Oleg's cafe does. She started with 148 chairs, and 3 were broken in a storm. She lent 126 chairs to the village fete. Oleg returned 18 chairs he had borrowed in the spring, and a house clearance added 25 more. A restaurant then bought 42 chairs from her. The cafe holds each booking for 90 minutes, and the board shows bookings in hours although the till records them in minutes. How many chairs does Tanya have now?

On Monday morning Alina cut 163 sheets of veneer, more than her partner Georg managed. Each sheet was sliced into 9 strips before noon. In the early afternoon every strip was cut into 7 tiles. Later 6074 tiles were laid on a hotel floor, and 1313 tiles cracked in the press. In the evening the factory produced 6 tiles for every tile still in the store. How many tiles are in the store now?

A wildlife park had 132 nesting boxes on its trees. A gale brought down 4 boxes, 79 were moved to a new reserve, and 12 were taken away for repair. The trust then built 7 boxes for every box still standing in the park. Over the winter squirrels destroyed 114 boxes, and the park covers 300 hectares. How many nesting boxes does the park have now?

Rafael prints more photographs than his assistant Nour does. He shot 75 rolls of film and bought 54 more from a colleague. Each roll produced 8 negatives, and every negative was printed at 7 different sizes. A flood in the darkroom ruined 539 prints. A gallery then ordered the whole surviving collection for each of its 4 venues, needing that many prints per venue. Half of the darkroom is unusable now, and the gallery has been open 22 years. How many prints does the gallery order come to?

On Wednesday morning a paint plant had 170 tins of base white, and 126 tins were used up on a hotel job. At midday a delivery doubled the number of tins in the store. During the afternoon the plant tinted 6 tins of colour from every tin of base. In the evening the depot ordered that whole batch for each of its 5 branches, needing that many tins per branch. The plant lists drying times in hours although the labels give them in minutes. How many tins were ordered altogether?

A taxi firm had 47 airport vouchers in the office. Drivers used 39 vouchers on Friday. The airport issued 30 fresh vouchers, and 12 expired at the end of the month. A hotel returned 9 unused vouchers. The airport then matched the office's stock, leaving it with 2 vouchers for every voucher it held. The firm quotes waiting times in minutes although the contract is written in hours. How many vouchers does the office have now?

Iris blends more tea than her colleague Owen does. She filled 203 boxes, and each box held 6 tins. Owen added 27 tins from his own bench. Every tin was then divided into 8 sachets for the school scheme, and each sachet was filled with 6 tea bags. Half of her warehouse is unheated, and the scheme measures its shelves in metres although the plans are drawn in centimetres. How many tea bags are in the scheme's sachets altogether?

A hardware chain ordered 152 cartons of light bulbs, and each carton held 9 bulbs. A returned order added 58 bulbs to the store. A hotel then bought 307 bulbs. A neighbouring shop lent the chain 29 bulbs, and the warehouse itself is 400 metres long. How many bulbs does the chain have?

A heritage railway printed 204 sheets of tickets, and each sheet made 4 tickets. During the summer 359 tickets were used up. A travel agent returned 63 unsold tickets, and the harbour office sent over 28 more. Half of the ticket hut is used as a store, and journeys are advertised in hours although the guards log them in minutes. How many tickets does the railway have?

Bianca keeps more ribbon in her studio than her student Rafi does. She began with 53 reels, and 13 reels were spoiled by damp. Rafi gave her 16 reels, and a market stall sold her 24 more. A wholesale offer then tripled the number of reels she held. Every reel was cut into 8 bows, and the bows were shared evenly into 2 identical stock boxes, of which the fair box is the one to follow. How many bows are in the fair box?

Nabila makes more cheese than her partner Emil does. She set 148 vats, and each vat produced 7 wheels. Mould spoiled 98 wheels, and Emil added 18 wheels from his own dairy. A supermarket contract then had the dairy scale up to 4 wheels for every wheel in the store. A neighbouring farm delivered 66 wheels, and the dairy weighs its milk in litres although the recipes are written in millilitres. How many wheels does the dairy have now?

A science lab ordered 132 crates of test tubes, and each crate held 7 tubes. The tubes were split evenly into 2 equal stores, and the annexe store is the one being followed. Breakages cost the annexe 136 tubes, and 290 tubes were transferred to another school. The supplier then delivered 8 tubes for every tube left in the annexe. The lab records reaction times in seconds although its reports are written in minutes. How many tubes are in the annexe store now?

Ellis owns more lanterns than his neighbour Rune does. He hung 38 lanterns along the lane and took half of them down when the storm warning came, leaving the rest up. The council then supplied 5 lanterns for every lantern still hanging. A gale destroyed 22 lanterns, and the festival committee donated 71 more. How many lanterns does Ellis have now?

A festival organiser had 143 tents in the store. A wedding hire took 85 tents away. A supplier then delivered 62 tents. The organiser ordered 4 tents for every tent in the store, and the following week scaled that up again to 7 tents for each of those. Half of the store is used for scaffolding, and the festival field holds 9000 people. How many tents does the final order come to?

Ada sells more woollen hats than her cousin Ravi does. She had 213 hats, and 196 of them were sold at the winter fair. Her workshop then made 5 hats for every hat she had left. The hats were shared equally between the 5 shops that stock her work, and the museum shop's share is the one being followed. That shop then ordered 9 hats for every hat in its share. How many hats does the museum shop's order come to?

A cycling club had 105 water bottles in its store, and a sponsor sent 22 more. A second sponsor then doubled the club's stock of bottles. A member donated 15 bottles, and 93 bottles were handed out at the sportive. A shop later returned 16 bottles that riders had left behind. How many bottles does the club have now?

A model railway club had 103 metres of track, and 68 metres were sold to a museum. Each metre still in the store was cut into 6 sections, and the sections were shared equally between the 5 layouts in the clubroom, with the harbour layout the one to follow. The club then ordered 9 replacement sections for every section on that layout. Those were split equally between the 6 members who build the harbour layout, and one member's share is followed from here. That member finally ordered 6 sections for each one in his share; half of the clubroom is taken up by that layout, and the club measures track in metres although the catalogue lists it in millimetres. How many sections does that member's final order come to?

On Monday morning Reza had 214 blank keyrings, more than his partner Silje had cut. Before noon the second press left the tray with 2 keyrings for every keyring on it. At midday the tray was split evenly into 2 equal batches, and the export batch is the one being followed. In the early afternoon the enamel line produced 3 keyrings for every keyring in that batch. Later the packing line made 5 for each of those, and in the evening a partner factory made 4 for each again. Silje then added 77 keyrings of her own, and the workshop has 18 benches. How many keyrings are in the export batch now?
